subject.title: feat(tui): inline image rendering via pi-tui Image component

question: Should TUI inline rendering ever read absolute MEDIA paths from the host process, or should it only render trusted structured image blocks and media-store references?
rationale: The feature is useful, but this branch crosses from model/tool text into host-local file reads and terminal graphics output, which is a product and security boundary choice rather than a mechanical repair.

options.title: Render trusted structured media only
options.body: Require the implementation to use current image blocks or structured generated-attachment/media-store references and avoid arbitrary absolute host path reads.

options.title: Allow constrained absolute MEDIA reads
options.body: Keep the PR's path-read shape only with an explicit trusted-root policy, focused tests, and live proof across local and Docker gateway setups.

options.title: Pause under the canonical issue
options.body: Keep the feature tracked in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/57592 while closing or parking this stale draft until a maintainer sponsors the boundary.

recommendation.title: Render trusted structured media only
recommendation.body: Require the implementation to use current image blocks or structured generated-attachment/media-store references and avoid arbitrary absolute host path reads.

likelyOwner.reason: The image_generate workflow and prior TUI inline-image routing both point to this owner as the best available decision candidate.
